metadata.title: Forking and stability in the representations of a $C^*$-algebra

extraction_notes.note: Fact \ref{HensonsLemma} (Henson's lemma) is cited in the proofs of Corollary 2.5 and of Theorem 3.6 but is never stated in the source; the \ref is unresolved and no node was created for it.

nodes.name: Representation of a unital C*-algebra
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra and let $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ be a $C^*$-algebra nondegenerate isometric homomorphism, where $B(H)$ is the algebra of bounded operators over a Hilbert space $H$.

nodes.name: Metric structure of a Hilbert space expanded by a C*-algebra
nodes.statement:
Recall that we include a symbol $\dot{a}$ in the language of the Hilbert space structure whose interpretation in $H$ will be $\pi(a)$ for every $a$ in the unit ball of $\mathcal{A}$ getting the following metric structure of only one sort: 
\[(Ball_1(H),0,-,i,\half[x+y],\|\cdot\|,(\pi(a))_{a\in Ball_1(\mathcal{A})})\] where $Ball_1(H)$  and $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ are the corresponding unit balls in $H$ and $\mathcal{A}$ respectively; $0$ is the zero vector in $H$; $-: Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to any vector $v\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $-v$; $i: Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the function that to any vector $v\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $iv$ where $i^2=-1$; $\half[x+y]: Ball_1(H)\times Ball_1(H)\to Ball_1(H)$ is the  function that to a couple of vectors $v$, $w\in Ball_1(H)$ assigns the vector $\half[v+w]$; $\|\cdot\|: Ball_1(H) \to [0, 1]$ is the norm function; $\mathcal{A}$ is an unital $C^*$-algebra; $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ is a $C^*$-algebra isometric homomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: The one-sorted metric structure on the unit ball of $H$ with zero, negation, multiplication by $i$, midpoint, norm, and the operators $\pi(a)$ for $a$ in the unit ball of $\mathcal{A}$.

nodes.name: Structure (H, pi)
nodes.statement: Briefly, the structure will be refered to as $(H,\pi)$.

nodes.name: Quantifier elimination for Th(H,pi)
nodes.statement: The theory of $(H,\pi)$ has quantifier elimination. Furthermore, for $v,w\in H$, $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\phi_v=\phi_w$. Here, $\phi_v:\mathcal{A}\to\ensuremath{\mathbb{C}}$ is the positive linear functional defined by the formula $\phi_v(a)=\langle av\ |\ v\rangle$.
conclusions: The theory of $(H,\pi)$ has quantifier elimination.
$tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\phi_v=\phi_w$
nodes.statement_short: Th(H,π) has quantifier elimination, and two vectors have the same type over ∅ iff they induce the same positive functional.

nodes.name: Characterization of orthogonality of stationary types
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$, $p,q\in S_1(E)$ be stationary and $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp_E q$ if and only if $\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_e)}\perp \phi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_e)}$, where the orthogonality of functionals is defined in Definition \ref{relationsbetweenpositivelinearfunctionals}.
assumptions: $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\perp_E q$ if and only if $\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(v_e)}\perp \phi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}(w_e)}$
nodes.statement_short: Stationary 1-types over E are orthogonal iff the functionals of the essential parts of their realizations' projections off acl(E) are orthogonal.

nodes.name: Subrepresentation generated by a set
nodes.statement: Given $E\subseteq H$ and $v\in H$, we denote by: \begin{itemize} \item $H_E$, the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by the elements $\pi(a)v$, where $v\in E$ and $a\in\mathcal{A}$. \item $\pi_E:=\{\pi(a)\upharpoonright H_E\ |\ a\in \mathcal{A}\}$. \item $(H_E,\pi_E)$, the subrepresentation of $(H,\pi)$ generated by $E$. \item $H_v$, the space $H_E$ when $E=\{v\}$ for some vector $v\in H$. \item $\pi_v:=\pi_E$ when $E=\{v\}$. \item $(H_v,\pi_v)$, the subrepresentation of $(H,\pi)$ generated by $v$. \item $(H,\pi,v)$, means that $\{\pi(a)v\ |\ a\in\mathcal{A}\}$ is dense in $(H,\pi)$. \item $H_E^\perp$, the orthogonal complement of $H_E$. \item $P_E$, the projection over $H_E$. \item $P_{E^\perp}$, the projection over $H_E^\perp$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Notation for the subrepresentation $H_E$ generated by a set $E$, its cyclic case $H_v$, orthogonal complements and projections.
nodes.label: DefinitionHv

nodes.name: Essential and discrete parts of a representation
nodes.statement: Given a representation $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$, we define: \begin{itemize} \item The \textit{essential part} of $\pi$ is the $C^*$-algebra homomorphism, \[\pi_e:=\rho\circ\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)\] of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$, where $\rho$ is the canonical proyection of $B(H)$ onto the Calkin Algebra $B(H)/\mathcal{K}(H)$. \item The \textit{discrete part} of $\pi$ is the restriction, \begin{align*} \pi_d:ker(\pi_e)&\to \mathcal{K}(H)\\ a &\to \pi(a) \end{align*} \item The \textit{discrete part} of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ is defined in the following way: \[\pi(\mathcal{A})_d:=\pi(\mathcal{A})\cap \mathcal{K}(H).\] \item The \textit{essential part} of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ is the image $\pi(\mathcal{A})_e$ of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ in the Calkin Algebra. \item The \textit{essential part} of $H$ is defined in the following way: \[H_e:=\text{ker}(\pi(\mathcal{A})_d)\] \item The \textit{discrete part} of $H$ is defined in the following way: \[H_d:=\text{ker}(\pi(\mathcal{A})_d)^\perp\] \item The \textit{essential part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_e$ of $v$ over $H_e$. \item The \textit{discrete part} of a vector $v\in H$ is the projection $v_d$ of $v$ over $H_d$. \item The \textit{essential part} of a set $E\subseteq H$ is the set \[E_e:=\{v_e\ |\ v\in E\}\] \item The \textit{discrete part} of a set $G\subseteq H$ is the set \[E_d:=\{v_d\ |\ v\in G\}\] \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Essential part via the Calkin algebra, discrete part via compact operators, for the representation, $\pi(\mathcal{A})$, $H$, vectors and sets.

nodes.name: Characterization of automorphisms fixing E
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$, $U\in \ensuremath{\text{Aut}}(H,\pi)$. Then $U\in \ensuremath{\text{Aut}}((H,\pi)/E)$ if and only if: \begin{itemize} \item For all $v\in H$ and all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $U(\pi(a)(v))=\pi(a)(Uv)$. \item For all $w\in H_E$, $Uw=w$. \end{itemize}
conclusions: $U\in \ensuremath{\text{Aut}}((H,\pi)/E)$ if and only if
nodes.statement_short: An automorphism fixes E iff it commutes with π(A) and fixes $H_E$ pointwise.
nodes.label: Aut(H/E)

nodes.name: Definable closure equals H_E
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Then $dcl(E)=H_E$
conclusions: $dcl(E)=H_E$
nodes.label: definclosure

nodes.name: Elementary equivalence with added essential part
nodes.statement: For any index set $I$, $(H,\pi)\equiv (H,\pi)\oplus(H_e,\pi_e)$.
conclusions: $(H,\pi)\equiv (H,\pi)\oplus(H_e,\pi_e)$
nodes.label: CoroElementaryEquivalent

nodes.name: Essential vectors are not algebraic over the empty set
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H_e$. Then $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.label: Henotalgebraicoveremptyset

nodes.name: Discrete vectors are algebraic over the empty set
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H_d$. Then $v$ is algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.label: Hdsubsetalgebraicclosureofemptyset

nodes.name: Vectors with nonzero essential part are not algebraic
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H$ such that $v_e\neq 0$. Then $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$.
conclusions: $v$ is not algebraic over $\emptyset$
nodes.label: LemmaIfVeNotZeroVNotAlgebraic

nodes.name: Algebraic closure of the empty set
nodes.statement: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
conclusions: $acl(\emptyset)=H_d$
nodes.label: aclemptyset

nodes.name: Algebraic closure of a set
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Then $acl(E)$ is the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$.
conclusions: $acl(E)$ is the Hilbert subspace of $H$ generated by $dcl(E)$ and $acl(\emptyset)$
nodes.label: aclE

nodes.name: Independence relation ind^*
nodes.statement: Let $E$, $F$, $G\subseteq H$. We say that $E$ is \textit{independent} from $G$ over $F$ if for all $v\in E$ $P_{acl(F)}(v)=P_{acl(F\cup G)}(v)$ and denote it $E\ind^*_F G$.
nodes.label: AindependentB

nodes.name: Characterizations of independence
nodes.statement: Let $\bar v$, $\bar w\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then it is easy to see that: \begin{itemize} \item $\bar v$ is independent from $\bar w$ over $\emptyset$ if and only if for every $j,k=1,\dots,n$, $H_{(v_j)_e}\perp H_{(w_k)_e}$. \item $\bar v$ is independent from $\bar w$ over $E$ if and only if for every $j,k=1,\dots,n$, $H_{P_E^\perp(v_j)_e}\perp H_{P_E^\perp(w_k)_e}$. \item $\bar v\in H^n$ and $E$, $F\subseteq H$. Then $\bar v\ind^*_EF$ if and only if for every $j=1,\dots,n$ $v_j\ind^*_EF$ that is, for all $j=1,\dots,n$ $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(E\cup F)}(v_j)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Independence of tuples reduces to orthogonality of the cyclic subspaces of essential parts, and to independence of each coordinate.
nodes.label: independenceoverempty

nodes.name: Types over the empty set via cyclic representations
nodes.statement: Let $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$. Then $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$, this is, the map sending $v$ to $w$ extends to a unique isometric isomorphism between $(H_v,\pi_v)$ and $(H_w,\pi_w)$.
conclusions: $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: typeoverempty1

nodes.name: Characterization of ind^*-independent extensions
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq F\subseteq H$, $p\in S_n(E)$ $q\in S_n(F)$ and $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)$, $\bar w=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ be such that $p=tp(\bar v/E)$ and $q=tp(\bar w/F)$. Then $q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bar w\ind^*_EF$ if and only if the following conditions hold: \begin{enumerate} \item For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $P_{acl(E)}(v_j)=P_{acl(F)}(w_j)$ \item For every $j=1,\dots,n$, $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_j)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w_j)$ \end{enumerate}
assumptions: be such that $p=tp(\bar v/E)$ and $q=tp(\bar w/F)$
conclusions: $q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bar w\ind^*_EF$ if and only if the following conditions hold
equivalent_conditions: $q$ is an extension of $p$ such that $\bar w\ind^*_EF$
nodes.statement_short: An extension q of p is $\ind^*$-independent iff the acl-projections agree and the cyclic representations of the parts orthogonal to acl are isomorphic.
nodes.label: nonforkingextension

nodes.name: Projection off acl(E) is the essential part of projection off E
nodes.statement: Recall that for every $E\subseteq H$ and $v\in H$, $P^\perp_{acl(E)}v=(P^\perp_Ev)_e$.

nodes.name: ind^* is a freeness relation
nodes.statement: $\ind^*$ is a freeness relation.
conclusions: $\ind^*$ is a freeness relation.
nodes.label: explicitnonforkingrelation

nodes.name: Stability via an independence relation
nodes.statement: A first order continuous logic theory $T$ is stable if and only if there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity. In that case the relation $\ind^*$ coincides with non-forking.
nodes.origin_citation: Ben Yaacov, Berenstein, Henson, Usvyatsov [BBHU], Theorem 14.14
assumptions: A first order continuous logic theory $T$
conclusions: $T$ is stable if and only if there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity
In that case the relation $\ind^*$ coincides with non-forking.
equivalent_conditions: there is an independence relation $\ind^*$ satisfying local character, finite character of dependence, transitivity, symmetry, invariance, existence and stationarity
nodes.label: LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation

nodes.name: Superstability of T_pi
nodes.statement: The theory $T_\pi$ is superstable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking.
conclusions: The theory $T_\pi$ is superstable
the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking
nodes.label: Tpisuperstable

nodes.name: Canonical base
nodes.statement: Recall that a canonical base for a type $p$ is a minimal set over which $p$ does not fork.

nodes.name: Canonical bases of types
nodes.statement: Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then $Cb(tp(\bar v/E)):=\{(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)\}$ is a canonical base for the type $tp(\bar v/E)$.
conclusions: $Cb(tp(\bar v/E)):=\{(P_Ev_1,\dots,P_Ev_n)\}$ is a canonical base for the type $tp(\bar v/E)$
also_stated_at: Let $\bar v\in H^n$ and $E\subseteq H$. Then the type $tp(\bar v/E)$ has a canonical base formed by a tuple of elements in $H$ and therefore, the theory of $(H,\pi)$ has weak elimination of imaginaries.
nodes.label: canonicalbase

nodes.name: Weak elimination of imaginaries for T_pi
nodes.statement: The theory $T_\pi$ has weak elimination of imaginaries.
conclusions: The theory $T_\pi$ has weak elimination of imaginaries.

nodes.name: Positive linear functional
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}^\prime$ be the dual space of $\mathcal{A}$. An element $\phi\in\mathcal{A}^\prime$ is called \textit{positive} if $\phi(a)\geq 0$ whenever $a\in\mathcal{A}$ is positive, i.e. there is $b\in\mathcal{A}$ such that $a=b^*b$. The set of positive functionals is denoted by $\mathcal{A}^\prime_+$.

nodes.name: Vector functionals are positive
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-algebra of operators on a Hilbert space $H$, and let $v\in H$. Then the function $\phi_v$ on $\mathcal{A}$ such that for every $S\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_v(S)=\langle Sv\,|\,v\rangle$ is a positive linear functional.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-algebra of operators on a Hilbert space $H$
conclusions: the function $\phi_v$ on $\mathcal{A}$ such that for every $S\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_v(S)=\langle Sv\,|\,v\rangle$ is a positive linear functional
nodes.label: vectorsdefinepositivelinearfunctionals

nodes.name: Types over the empty set via positive functionals
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. Then $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\phi_v=\phi_w$, where $\phi_v$ denotes the positive linear functional on $\mathcal{A}$ defined by $v$ as in Lemma \ref{vectorsdefinepositivelinearfunctionals}.
conclusions: $tp(v/\emptyset)=tp(w/\emptyset)$ if and only if $\phi_v=\phi_w$
nodes.label: typeoverempty4

nodes.name: Orthogonality and domination of positive functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$. \begin{enumerate} \item They are called \textit{orthogonal} ($\phi\perp\psi$) if $\|\phi-\psi\|=\|\phi\|+\|\psi\|$. \item Also, $\phi$ is called \textit{dominated} by $\psi$ ($\phi\leq\psi$) if there exist $\gamma>0$ such that the functional $\gamma\psi-\phi$ is positive. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\phi\perp\psi$ when $\|\phi-\psi\|=\|\phi\|+\|\psi\|$; $\phi\leq\psi$ when $\gamma\psi-\phi$ is positive for some $\gamma>0$.
nodes.label: relationsbetweenpositivelinearfunctionals

nodes.name: Subrepresentation criterion via domination
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. Then $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$ if and only if $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$.
conclusions: $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$ if and only if $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$
equivalent_conditions: $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: HvinHw

nodes.name: Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ be a positive functional on $\mathcal{A}$. Then there exists a cyclic representation $(H_\phi,\pi_\phi,v_\phi)$ such that for all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi(a)=\langle \pi_\phi(a)v_\phi|v_\phi\rangle$. This representation is called the \textit{Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction}.
conclusions: there exists a cyclic representation $(H_\phi,\pi_\phi,v_\phi)$ such that for all $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi(a)=\langle \pi_\phi(a)v_\phi|v_\phi\rangle$
nodes.label: GelfandNaimarkSegal

nodes.name: Orthogonal functionals give non-embeddable representations
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. If $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$, then $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$.
conclusions: $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to any subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic

nodes.name: Disjoint representations
nodes.statement: Recall that two representations are said to be \textit{disjoint} if they do not have any common subrepresentation up to isometric isomorphism.
differentia: they do not have any common subrepresentation up to isometric isomorphism

nodes.name: Disjoint subrepresentations have separating central projection
nodes.statement: Two subrepresentations $(H_1,\pi_1)$, $(H_2,\pi_2)$ of $(H,\pi)$ are disjoint if and only if there is a projection $P$ in $\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap \pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are the projections on $H_1$ and $H_2$ respectively, we have that $PP_1=P_1$ and $(I-P)P_2=P_2$.
conclusions: are disjoint if and only if there is a projection $P$ in $\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap \pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$
nodes.label: FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections

nodes.name: Strong closure is the double commutant
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$algebra and $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ a nondegenerate representation of $\mathcal{A}$. Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ be the strong closure of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$. Then $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is weakly closed and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$algebra and $\pi:\mathcal{A}\to B(H)$ a nondegenerate representation of $\mathcal{A}$
Let $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ be the strong closure of $\pi(\mathcal{A})$.
conclusions: $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$ is weakly closed and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}=\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}$
nodes.label: FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA

nodes.name: Kaplansky density theorem
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-subalgebra of $B(H)$ with strong closure $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$. Then the unit ball $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ is strongly dense in the unit ball $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$. Furthermore, the set of selfadjoint elements in $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ is strongly dense in the set of selfadjoint elements of $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ be a $C^*$-subalgebra of $B(H)$ with strong closure $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$
conclusions: the unit ball $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ is strongly dense in the unit ball $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$ of $\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}}$
the set of selfadjoint elements in $Ball_1(\mathcal{A})$ is strongly dense in the set of selfadjoint elements of $Ball_1(\ensuremath{\mathcal{M}})$
nodes.label: TheoremKaplansky

nodes.name: Approximate characterization of orthogonal functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be two positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$. Then, $\phi\perp\psi$ if and only if for all $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\psi(a)<\epsilon$.
assumptions: $\phi$ and $\psi$ be two positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$
conclusions: $\phi\perp\psi$ if and only if for all $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\psi(a)<\epsilon$
equivalent_conditions: for all $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\psi(a)<\epsilon$
nodes.label: phiperppsi

nodes.name: Orthogonality passes to dominated functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\phi_1$, $\phi_2$, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ be positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\phi_1\leq\phi_2$ and $\psi_1\leq\psi_2$. If $\phi_2\perp\psi_2$, then $\phi_1\perp\psi_1$.
assumptions: $\phi_1$, $\phi_2$, $\psi_1$ and $\psi_2$ be positive linear functionals on $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\phi_1\leq\phi_2$ and $\psi_1\leq\psi_2$
conclusions: $\phi_1\perp\psi_1$
nodes.label: phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2

nodes.name: Orthogonal functionals iff disjoint cyclic representations
nodes.statement: Let $v,w\in H$. $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$ if and only if no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$.
conclusions: $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$ if and only if no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
equivalent_conditions: no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$
nodes.label: HvperpHw

nodes.name: Almost orthogonality of types over the empty set
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{v_e}\perp \phi_{w_e}$.
assumptions: $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{v_e}\perp \phi_{w_e}$
nodes.label: orthogonalityoverempty

nodes.name: Almost orthogonality of types over E
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$, let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\perp_E^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{P^\perp_E(v_e)}\perp \phi_{P^\perp_E(w_e)}$
assumptions: $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\perp_E^a q$ if and only if $\phi_{P^\perp_E(v_e)}\perp \phi_{P^\perp_E(w_e)}$
nodes.label: orthogonalityoverA

nodes.name: Almost orthogonality equals orthogonality
nodes.statement: Let $E\subseteq H$. Let $p,q\in S_1(E)$. Then, $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $p\perp q$.
conclusions: $p\perp^a q$ if and only if $p\perp q$

nodes.name: Domination of types over the empty set
nodes.statement: Let $p,q\in S_1(\emptyset)$ and let $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$. Then, $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$ if and only if $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$.
assumptions: $v$, $w\in H$ be such that $v\models p$ and $w\models q$
conclusions: $p\vartriangleright_\emptyset q$ if and only if $\phi_{w_e}\leq\phi_{v_e}$
nodes.label: dominationoverempty

nodes.name: Domination of stationary types
nodes.statement: Let $E$, $F$ and $G$ be small subsets of $\tilde{H}$ such that $E$, $F\subseteq G$ and $p\in S_1(E)$ and $q\in S_1(F)$ be two stationary types. Then $p\vartriangleright_G q$ if and only if there exist $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$ such that $tp(v/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $p$, $tp(w/G)$ is a non-forking extension of $q$ and $\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}w_e}\leq\phi_{P^\perp_{acl(G)}v_e}$.
assumptions: $E$, $F$ and $G$ be small subsets of $\tilde{H}$ such that $E$, $F\subseteq G$
$p\in S_1(E)$ and $q\in S_1(F)$ be two stationary types
conclusions: $p\vartriangleright_G q$ if and only if there exist $v$, $w\in\tilde{H}$ such that

Then, by Fact \ref{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\pi}):=(H,\pi)\oplus (H^\prime,\pi^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\pi)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$.
			\item[Induction step] Now, let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in \tilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$.

nodes.statement: Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, there exists $q\in S_n(F)$ such that $q$ is a non-forking extension of $p$.

nodes.name: Base case: add a copy of the orthogonal part and apply Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement: [Case $n=1$] Let $v\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$ and let $(H^\prime,\pi^\prime,u):=(H_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},\pi_{(P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$. Then, by Fact \ref{HensonsLemma}, the model $(\hat{H},\hat{\pi}):=(H,\pi)\oplus (H^\prime,\pi^\prime)$ is an elementary extension of $(H,\pi)$. Let $v^\prime:=P_{acl(E)}v+P^\perp_{acl(E)}v_d+u\in \hat{H}$. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, the type $tp(v^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v/E)$.

nodes.name: Inductive step via an automorphism and transitivity
nodes.statement: [Induction step] Now, let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})\in \tilde{H}^{n+1}$. By induction hypothesis, there are $v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime\in H$ such that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$. Let $v_{n+1}^\prime\in \tilde{H}$ be such that $tp(v_{n+1}^\prime/Fv_1^\prime\cdots v_n^\prime)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(U(v_{n+1})/Ev_1^\prime,\cdots v_n^\prime)$. Then, by transitivity, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime,v_{n+1}^\prime/F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}/E)$.

nodes.name: Stationarity
nodes.statement:
[Stationarity] Let $(\tilde{H},\tilde{\pi})$ be the monster model and let $E\subseteq F\subseteq \tilde{H}$ be small sets. We show, by induction on $n$, that for every $p\in S_n(E)$, if $q\in S_n(F)$ is a $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ then $q=p^\prime$, where $p^\prime$ is the $\ind^*$-independent extension of $p$ to $F$ built in the proof of existence.
		\begin{description}
			\item[Case $n=1$] Let $v\in H$ be such that $p=tp(v/E)$, and let $q\in S(F)$ and $w\in H$ be such that $w\models q$. Let $v^\prime$ be as in previous item. Then, by Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} we have that:
		       \begin{enumerate}
        	   	\item $P_{acl(E)}v=P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$
			    \item $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(E)}v},P^\perp_{acl(E)}v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to both 
\[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)\]
 and 
\[(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)\]
			    \end{enumerate}
This means that $P_{acl(F)}v^\prime=P_{acl(F)}w$ and $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}w},P^\perp_{acl(F)}w)$ is isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},\pi_{P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime},P^\perp_{acl(F)}v^\prime)$ and, therefore $q=tp(v^\prime/F)=p^\prime$.
			\item[Induction step] Let $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1})$, $\bar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n,v_{n+1}^\prime)$ and $\bar w=(w_1,\dots,w_{n+1})\in\tilde{H}$ be such that $\bar v\models p$, $\bar v^\prime\models p^\prime$ and $\bar w\models q$. By transitivity, we have that $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)$ and $tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_1,\dots,v_n/E)$. By induction hypothesis, $tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n/F)$. Let $U$ be an automorphism of the monster model fixing $E$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U(v_j)=v_j^\prime$ and let $U^\prime$ an automorphism of the monster model fixing $F$ pointwise such that for every $j=1,\dots,n$, $U^\prime(v_j^\prime)=w_j^\prime$. Again by transitivity, $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)$ and $tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ are $\ind^*$-independent extensions of $tp(v_{n+1}/Ev_1,\cdots v_n)$. By the case $n=1$ $tp(U^{-1}(v_{n+1}^\prime)/Fv_1\cdots v_n)=tp((U^\prime\circ U)^{-1}(w_{n+1})/Fv_1,\cdots v_n)$ and therefore $p^\prime=tp(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime v_{n+1}^\prime/F)=tp(w_1,\dots,w_n,w_{n+1}/F)=q$.

nodes.name: Proof of Superstability of T_pi
nodes.statement: By Fact \ref{LemmaTstableIffItHasGoodIndependenceRelation}, $T_\pi$ is stable and the relation $\ind^*$ agrees with non-forking. To prove superstability, we have to show that for every $\bar v=(v_1,\dots,v_n)\in H$, every $F\subseteq H$ and every $\epsilon>0$, there exist a finite $F_0\subseteq F$ and $\bar v^\prime=(v_1^\prime,\dots,v_n^\prime)\in H^n$ such that $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\epsilon$ and $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}F$ for every $j\leq n$. As in the proof of local character, for $j=1,\dots,n$ let $(\ a_1^{jk},\dots,\ a_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$, $(\ e_1^{jk},\dots,\ e_{l_k}^{jk})_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$, $w_j:=(P_{acl(E)}(v_j))_e$ and $(w_j^k)_{k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ be such that $w_j^k:=\sum_{s=1}^{l_k}\pi(a_s^{jk})\ e_s^{jk}$ for $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$, and $w_j^k\to w_j$. For $j=1,\dots,n$, let $K_j\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ be such that $\|w_j-w_j^{K_j}\|<\epsilon$, let $v_j^\prime:=(P_{acl(E)}v_j)_d+w_j^{K_j}$ and let $F_0^j=\{e_s^k\ |\ k\leq K_j\text{ and }s=1,\dots,l_k\}$. If we define $F_0:=U_{j=1}^nF_0^j$, then for every $j=1,\dots,n$ we have that $v_j^\prime\ind_{F_0}^*F$, $|F_0|<\aleph_0$ and $\|v_j-v_j^\prime\|<\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Canonical bases of types
nodes.statement: First of all, we consider the case of a 1-tuple. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension} $tp(v/E)$ does not fork over $Cb(tp(v/E))$. Let $(v_k)_{k<\omega}$ a Morley sequence for $tp(v/E)$. We have to show that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. By Theorem \ref{nonforkingextension}, for every $k<\omega$ there is a vector $w_k$ such that $v_k=P_Ev+w_k$ and $w_k\perp acl(\{P_Ev\}\cup\{w_j\ |\ j< k\})$. This means that for every $k<\omega$, $w_k\in H_e$ and for all $j$, $k<\omega$, $H_{w_j}\perp H_{w_k}$. For $k<\omega$, let $v^\prime_k:=\frac{v_1+\cdots+v_k}{n}=P_Ev+\frac{w_1+\cdots+w_k}{n}$. Then for every $k<\omega$, $v^\prime_k\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. Since $v^\prime_k\to P_ev$ when $k\to\infty$, we have that $P_Ev\in dcl((v_k)_{k<\omega})$. For the case of a general $n$-tuple, by Remark \ref{RemarkItIsEnoughIndependenceForOneVector}, it is enough to repeat the previous argument in every component of $\bar v$.
nodes.statement_short: For 1-tuples, show $P_Ev$ is definable from a Morley sequence via averages; the $n$-tuple case is coordinatewise.

nodes.name: Proof of Subrepresentation criterion via domination
nodes.statement: Suppose $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then there exists a vector $v^\prime\in H_w$ such that $(H_v,\pi_v,v)\simeq (H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$. By Radon Nikodim Theorem for rings of operators (see \cite{Hen}), there exists a bounded positive operator $P:(H_w,\pi_w,w)\to (H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ such that $Pw=v^\prime$ and $P$ commutes with every element of $\pi_v(\mathcal{A})$. Let $\gamma=\|P\|^2$. Then, for every positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$, $\phi_{v}(a)=\phi_{v^\prime}(a)=\langle \pi(a)v^\prime\ |\ v^\prime\rangle=\langle \pi(a)Pw\ |\ Pw\rangle=\langle P^*\pi(a)Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle \pi(a)\|P\|^2w\ |\ w\rangle\leq \gamma\langle \pi(a)w\ |\ w\rangle=\gamma\phi_{w}(a)$ which means that $\gamma\phi_w-\phi_{v}$ is positive and $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$. The converse is Corollary 3.3.8 in \cite{Pe}.
nodes.statement_short: Forward: Radon-Nikodym gives a positive operator bounding $\phi_v$ by $\|P\|^2\phi_w$; converse cited from Pedersen.

nodes.name: Proof of Orthogonal functionals give non-embeddable representations
nodes.statement: Suppose $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$, and $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. By Theorem \ref{HvinHw} $\phi_v\leq\phi_w$; let $\gamma>0$ be a real number such that $\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$ is a bounded positive functional and let $u\in H$ be such that $\phi_u=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_v$, which is possible by GNS Theorem. Then $\phi_v=\gamma\phi_w-\phi_u$, and $\|\phi_w-\phi_v\|=\|\phi_w-\gamma\phi_w+\phi_u\|=\|(1-\gamma)\phi_w+\phi_u\|=|1-\gamma|\|\phi_w\|+\|\phi_u\|\neq \|\phi_w\|+\|\phi_v\|$, but this contradicts $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: domination via Theorem 4.5 and GNS yields a norm identity incompatible with orthogonality.

nodes.name: Proof of Orthogonality passes to dominated functionals
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_1>0$ and $\gamma_2>0$ be such that $\gamma_1\phi_2-\phi_1$ and $\gamma_2\psi_2-\psi_1$ are positive. nodes.name: Proof of Orthogonal functionals iff disjoint cyclic representations
nodes.statement: Suppose $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$. By Lemma \ref{phi1lessthanphi2perppsi1lessthatpsi2}, if $(H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ and $(H_{w^\prime},\pi_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$ is a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$, then $\phi_{v^\prime}\perp\phi_{w^\prime}$, By Lemma \ref{phivperpphiwnotismoetricallyisomorphic}, $(H_{v^\prime},\pi_{v^\prime},v^\prime)$ is not isometrically isomorphic to $(H_{w^\prime},\pi_{w^\prime},w^\prime)$, and the conclusion follows. Conversely, suppose no subrepresentation of $(H_v,\pi_v,v)$ is isometrically isomorphic to a subrepresentation of $(H_w,\pi_w,w)$. Then the representations $(H_v,\pi_v)$ and $(H_w,\pi_w)$ are disjoint. By Fact \ref{FactDisjointSubrepresentationsHaveDisjointProjections}, there is a projection $P\in\pi(\mathcal{A})^\prime\cap\pi(\mathcal{A})^{\prime\prime}$ such that $PP_v=P_v$ and $(I-P)P_w=P_w$. Then, $\phi_v(I-P)=\langle (I-P)v\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-PP_vv)\ |\ v\rangle=\langle (v-v)\ |\ v\rangle=0$. On the other hand, $\phi_w(P)=\langle Pw\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(w-Pw)\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)w\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-(I-P)P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-P_ww\ |\ w\rangle=\langle w-w\ |\ w\rangle=0$. By Fact \ref{FactMMisDoubleCommutantOfPiOfA} and Theorem \ref{TheoremKaplansky}, the projection $P$ is strongly approximable by positive elements in $\pi(\mathcal{A})$ and therefore, for $\epsilon>0$ there exists a positive element $a\in\mathcal{A}$ with norm less than or equal to $1$, such that $\phi_v(e-a)<\epsilon$ and $\phi_w(a)<\epsilon$. By Fact \ref{phiperppsi}, $\phi_v\perp\phi_w$.
